title: Lajja
author: Taslima Nasrin
current_text: The Bangladeshi government banned Lajja in 1993 on the grounds that it had “created misunderstanding between communities”; writers and human rights activists publicly protested the ban.

sources.quote: In July, after months of pressure, the Bangladeshi government banned the book on the grounds that it had “created misunderstanding between communities.” The ban, seen as a sign of the growing influence of religious extremists, was publicly protested by many writers and human rights activists.

Events began with the 1993 publication of Lajja / Shame, a novel set in the backdrop of anti-Hindu riots in Bangladesh in the aftermath of the Babri Mosque demolition by right-wing Hindu activists in India. The last page of the novel portrays the Hindu protagonist leaving Bangladesh for India: Bangladesh was no longer home to non-Muslims, that was the bleak message of the novel’s finale. The government immediately banned the book.
sources.title: We Wish to Inform You: Censorship in Bangladesh (1972-2024)
